supplied: return (1) the largest pet weight (`Pets.weight`) in the group ...; (2) type of pet (`Pets.PetType`)
difference: The submission returns the columns in the order "SELECT PetType, MAX(weight) ...", giving ['cat', 12.0]. The gold uses "SELECT max(weight), petType", giving [12.0, 'cat']. The values match, but the column order is reversed, so the row tuples don't match.
question_gap: yes — the question says "List the maximum weight and pet type", which gives the gold's column order. The agent reversed it.

supplied: return (1) car make and model name (`car_names.Make`); (2) model year (`cars_data.Year`)
difference: The submission reads "maker" as car_makers.Maker/FullName: it joins model_list and car_makers, returns "cm.Maker, cm.FullName, cd.Year" and adds "ORDER BY cd.Id ASC LIMIT 1", giving [['gm','General Motors',1970]]. The gold returns "T2.Make, T1.Year" from car_names for all 35 cars from 1970, with no LIMIT.
question_gap: no — "maker" points more naturally to the car_makers table than to car_names.Make, which is a model name. The singular "the carr" also suggests one row, while the gold returns all 35 cars tied for the earliest year.

supplied: equals Source Airport (`flights.SourceAirport`) (compared as text, character by character)
difference: The submission joins on "TRIM(f.SourceAirport) = a.AirportCode", so codes that would otherwise not match do match, and it returns [['Albany ', 57]]. It also adds an extra column, COUNT(f.FlightNo). The gold uses an exact match, "T1.AirportCode = T2.SourceAirport", which matches nothing and returns 0 rows.
question_gap: no — the question gives no hint that untrimmed codes should fail to match. The gold's empty result comes from a data quirk, and the agent's TRIM is a reasonable fix for it.

supplied: return (1) airline name (`airlines.Airline`); ... keep only the first 1 rows
difference: The submission has no LIMIT and adds a flight_count column. It groups by f.Airline and returns all 12 airlines with their counts, e.g. ['United Airlines', 100]. The gold has "LIMIT 1" and returns only the name, ['Virgin America']. Several airlines are tied at 100 flights.
question_gap: partly — "What airline" implies one name and no count. But because of the 100-flight ties, the specific airline the gold returns is arbitrary.

supplied: return (1) the number of records in the group; (2) employee city or team (`employee.City`)
difference: The submission returns "SELECT City, COUNT(*)", giving ['Bath', 3]. The gold uses "SELECT count(*), city", giving [3, 'Bath']. The values match, but the column order is reversed.
question_gap: partly — "number of employees from each city" names the count first, which loosely suggests the gold's order. It doesn't state a column order.

supplied: for each result row, return (1) employee city or team (`employee.City`)
difference: Submitted added an extra column, "COUNT(*) as employee_count", and returned [['Bath', 2]]. Gold selects only "city" and returns [['Bath']]. The filter, grouping and HAVING clause are the same.
question_gap: yes; the question asks only to 'find the cities', so the count column is extra.

supplied: return (1) teacher age (`teacher.Age`); (2) teacher hometown district (`teacher.Hometown`)
difference: Submitted added an extra column, "Name" ("SELECT Name, Age, Hometown"). Gold has "SELECT Age, Hometown". The rows are otherwise the same.
question_gap: yes; the question names exactly two attributes, age and hometown.

supplied: return (1) the number of records in the group; (2) playing hand (`players.hand`)
difference: Submitted puts the columns in the order "hand, COUNT(*)", giving ['', 954]. Gold uses "count(*), hand", giving [954, '']. The values are the same; only the column order differs, and the grader is sensitive to it.
question_gap: no; the question doesn't fix the column order, and the hand-then-count order is just as natural.

supplied: return (1) episode title (`TV_series.Episode`); order the result rows by household rating (`TV_series.Rating`) ascending in character order
difference: Submitted added extra columns ("CAST(Rating AS REAL) as numeric_rating, Air_Date, Channel"), a "WHERE Rating IS NOT NULL" filter, and "ORDER BY CAST(Rating AS REAL) DESC". Gold is "SELECT Episode FROM TV_series ORDER BY rating". The failure comes from the extra columns, because grading compares rows as sets and ignores order.
question_gap: partly; 'all of the episodes' implies returning only the episodes, but the question doesn't say which direction to sort, and the sort direction doesn't affect grading anyway.

supplied: return (1) final tables made (`poker_player.Final_Table_Made`); (2) best finishing position (`poker_player.Best_Finish`)
difference: Submitted added a join to people plus extra columns "pp.Poker_Player_ID, p.Name". Gold selects only "Final_Table_Made, Best_Finish". The values in those two columns are the same.
question_gap: yes; the question asks only for final tables made and best finishes.

supplied: form of government (`country.GovernmentForm`) equals 'Republic' (compared as text, character by character)
difference: Submitted used "GovernmentForm LIKE '%Republic%'", which also matches values such as 'Federal Republic' and 'Islamic Republic' and returned 51.0612. Gold uses "GovernmentForm = \"Republic\"" and returns 50.8435.
question_gap: partly -- 'republics' could mean only the exact stored value 'Republic' or every government form that contains 'Republic'; the question does not say which, and gold uses the exact value.

supplied: Start from each `country` record; group the kept records by form of government
difference: Submitted added "WHERE LifeExpectancy IS NOT NULL". This drops countries with no life expectancy from the population sum, so 'Dependent Territory of the UK' gives 191000 instead of gold's 193050. It also returned the columns as (GovernmentForm, SUM) instead of gold's (sum, GovernmentForm).
question_gap: yes -- the question asks for total population per government form, and nothing in it suggests leaving out countries that have no life-expectancy value.
